findings.claim: GetEqualityComparer<T> used to throw TypeAccessException for types with no known hash-resistant comparer when UntrustedData is active. It now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default. This silently disables the collision-resistance protection: an attacker can send hash-colliding keys for any non-whitelisted key type (custom structs, classes) in Dictionary/HashSet and cause a hash-flooding DoS. The change is unrelated to the requirement and breaks a secure-by-default behavior.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a Dictionary<CustomKey,int> (CustomKey is a user type with no hash-resistant comparer) with MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData. Base throws TypeAccessException; head succeeds with the default comparer. Existing tests asserting TypeAccessException (e.g. in MessagePackSecurityTests) should fail on head. Mutation: reverting the line is killed by that test.

findings.claim: Surrogate mode lets string keys come from KeyAttribute, but the member-name match uses only the first member with that name. The new generated-formatter path reads and writes members without checking MsgPack-level restrictions on the target (for example, it gives no diagnostic for init-only or required members, and passes empty constructorParameters). A struct or class lacking a settable path could emit code that fails to compile or leaves required members unset. This is mainly a correctness risk, with a minor security impact from partially initialized objects.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a snapshot test with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] over a type with a required or init-only public property and run the generator tests to see whether the output compiles and whether required members are set.
